subject: Cloud Computing
title: The $72,000 Mistake
description: A micro-lesson that makes The $72,000 Mistake usable.

hook.text: A developer left a GPU instance running over a holiday weekend. The bill: $72,000 for three days.

buildup.text: GPU instances cost $3-$30 per hour. Forget to shut one down and the meter runs — 24 hours a day.

discovery.text: Billing alerts and budgets can warn you before costs spiral. Most providers let you set spending thresholds.

twist.text: Cloud providers won't stop your spending automatically. Alerts only warn — they don't turn anything off.

climax.text: Companies now build automated kill switches: if spending exceeds a limit, resources shut down automatically.

punchline.text: The cloud never stops charging. Even on holidays.

quiz.question: What is a critical limitation of cloud billing alerts?
options: They warn about spending but don't automatically stop resources from running
They only work for storage costs, not compute
They take two weeks to notify you of overspending

details.summary: Cloud horror stories of accidental bills ranging from thousands to hundreds of thousands of dollars are common. Causes include forgotten GPU instances, misconfigured auto-scaling, leaked API keys enabling crypto mining, and accidental deployment to expensive regions.
details.whyItMatters: A single misconfiguration can generate a devastating bill in hours. Understanding common causes and implementing guardrails protects organizations from financially catastrophic cloud mistakes.
takeaways: Forgotten GPU instances can cost thousands per day
Leaked credentials enable crypto mining on your account
Budget alerts and spending caps are essential safeguards

faq.question: How do you prevent accidental large cloud bills?
faq.answer: Set budget alerts at multiple thresholds. Enable billing anomaly detection. Restrict expensive instance types with IAM policies. Use service control policies to block unnecessary regions. Review bills weekly. Never hardcode credentials in code repositories.

faq.question: Will cloud providers forgive accidental charges?
faq.answer: Providers sometimes issue one-time courtesy credits for accidental charges, especially for new accounts. AWS, Azure, and GCP all have processes to request relief. However, this is discretionary, not guaranteed, and typically only happens once per account.
